title: Preserving CUDA Syntax for SYCL Portability: A Thin C++ Abstraction without Kernel Migration
problem: Large-scale scientific applications must support multiple GPU architectures (NVIDIA, Intel), but converting CUDA code to SYCL requires significant effort and risks introducing bugs. Existing approaches either require full code translation or accept performance penalties.
motivation: GPU hardware diversity (NVIDIA CUDA, Intel SYCL) forces developers to choose between single-vendor lock-in or expensive multi-backend maintenance. Need for practical portability solutions that preserve existing CUDA investments while enabling new architectures.
method: A thin wrapper layer in C++ keeps your original CUDA kernel code (the GPU commands written for NVIDIA) readable and runnable while making it work with SYCL (a portable GPU framework that runs on multiple brands). The approach mechanically converts kernels into function objects—a process called 'functorization'—without forcing you to rewrite the source code by hand. The team tested it on CRK-HACC, an N-body cosmology simulation (a program that models how gravity pulls many objects around), running the same code on both Polaris (NVIDIA GPUs) and Aurora (Intel GPUs). The system preserves architecture-specific optimizations, so you keep the speed tweaks you've made for each GPU type.
key_novelty: The innovation is a wrapper that lets you keep your CUDA code exactly as-is and compile it for both NVIDIA and Intel GPUs, avoiding code duplication and automated translation while preserving your kernel structure and performance optimizations.
contributions: Unified kernel abstraction preserving CUDA syntax
Mechanical functorization process for SYCL conversion
Single-source compilation for CUDA and SYCL
Case study on production cosmology code (CRK-HACC)
